messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Patient Information: 
Name: Not specified
Age: 62
Gender: Male

Hospital Course: 
The patient was admitted to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain and distension for the past month, which worsened in the last five days. The patient was diagnosed with small intestinal obstruction and underwent emergency laparotomy. During the operation, a small amount of food fiber was expelled, and multiple “stenosis rings” were found in the intestinal lumen at approximately 40 cm from the distal obstruction. The diseased bowel was removed, and the patient recovered without any discomfort. Pathological findings reported intestinal stenosis, mucosal erosion, and inflammatory granulation tissue formation. It showed neutrophil infiltration and vasodilation and congestion in the serosa. The muscle layer and serosa layer did not show any structural abnormality.

Summary of Hospital Stay: 
The patient was admitted to the hospital with abdominal pain and distension for the past month and was diagnosed with small intestinal obstruction. The patient underwent emergency laparotomy, and a diseased bowel was removed. The pathological findings reported intestinal stenosis and mucosal erosion. The patient recovered well without any discomfort. 
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Condition at Discharge: 
Recovered.

Follow-up Plan: 
Patient was followed up for two months, and no discomfort was found. No further treatment is required at this time.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Multiple mucosal "stenosis rings" with erosion and inflammatory granulation tissue caused a small-bowel obstruction, which was treated by laparotomy and resection. That makes an intestinal obstruction due to stricture or stenosis of the small intestine the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, in chapter K. ICD-10-AM classes stenosis or stricture of the intestine causing obstruction under other intestinal obstruction, category K56, rather than K56.4 for food-bolus impaction, because the stenosis caused the impaction.

CODE: K56
